html:
The Nurek Dam is an earth-fill dam on the Vakhsh River in Tajikistan, built from 1961 to 1980. At about 300 metres it was the tallest dam in the world for decades, and it is still the second tallest made by people.

The Soviet Union built it for power and irrigation. Its power station, with its first turbine running in 1972, produces about 3,000 megawatts and for years supplied most of Tajikistan's electricity, including the huge aluminium smelter at Tursunzoda. Water from its reservoir also irrigates cotton fields.

China's Jinping I dam is now slightly taller, and the Rogun Dam being built upstream on the Vakhsh will be taller still. Nature made an even higher one nearby, the Usoi landslide dam in the Pamirs. Dams on the rivers that feed the Amu Darya cause tension with Uzbekistan downstream, which fears for the water of its cotton fields.
